newsitem.title: USA: Patterson says strong U.S. results offset Canada.
newsitem.headline: Patterson says strong U.S. results offset Canada.

text.p: Patterson Dental Co said strong U.S. performance in the fourth quarter and fiscal 1997 offset mostly flat sales and margin pressure in Canada.

"U.S. operations ... were very strong for the fourth quarter and fiscal year -- more than compensating for the continued challenges presented by our Canadian operation," said Peter Frechette, chief executive of the largest North American dental products distributor.
Sales in Canada were essentially flat and margin pressure in that market led to a Canadian loss of $678,000, or $0.03 per share, for fiscal 1997, Patterson reported.
"We are working to reduce expenses at this operation in an effort to offset the impact of the soft market environment," Frechette said.
For the fourth quarter ended April 26, Patterson reported overall net income of $9.3 million, up from $8.4 million a year ago. Sales were $181.4 million versus $155.2 million.

For the year, the company posted net income of $32.4 million compared with $28.7 million a year earlier. Net sales for fiscal 1997 were $661.5 million, up 13.7 percent compared with $581.9 million in the same period a year ago. Gross margin rose to 35.9 percent versus 35.3 percent last year.
Frechette said, "The company's favorable momentum appears to be continuing into fiscal 1998."
